name: Notes and knowledge base
intro: Where a thought lands instantly and never gets lost, and where the app lags.

apps.title: 1Writer - Markdown Text Editor
apps.verdict: A clean, reliable Markdown editor with Dropbox and iCloud support, an extended keyboard, and an actions system. Used for years as a trusted mobile node in personal knowledge management setups. Rarely breaks, sync just works.
apps.loved: Lightning-fast full-text search across all Dropbox files. The extended keyboard with Markdown buttons speeds up typing.
apps.weak: No OneDrive or Google Drive support: only Dropbox and iCloud. A custom iCloud folder is not directly accessible by default. Updates are rare, though the stability compensates for it.
apps.whoFor: Developers, researchers, and technical writers building a plain-text knowledge base synced via Dropbox or iCloud.

quotes.text: I feel like I've downloaded (and bought!) nearly every writing, notes, and markdown app that is available for iOS. Sometimes I want something to take quick notes and with quick search to find them. Then I want something to compose longer material.

I love this app. Navigation is great, it supports [[backlinking]], ![embeds](), and #tags like a champ. I use Obsidian with iCloud and this pulls in all of my files with ease. My favorite feature is the customizable markdown extended keyboard.

apps.title: Granola - AI Meeting Notes
apps.verdict: The best meeting recorder in the sample: transcription is accurate, summaries are structured and substantive. Runs in the background without getting in the way. Weaker on mobile than desktop: transcription quality drops in noisy in-person settings. Requires a Google account, which turns some users away.
apps.loved: The meeting summary is ready immediately after the call ends and includes real action items, not vague generalities. You can add your own notes during recording and they get woven into the final document. Works with multiple languages simultaneously.
apps.weak: Struggles with in-person meetings in noisy environments on mobile. Full functionality requires a Google account. The mobile interface is noticeably less responsive than the desktop version.
apps.whoFor: Managers, doctors, and consultants who need to be present in a meeting rather than taking notes.

quotes.text: I've tried many meeting recorder and note-taking tool out there, and nothing comes close. The transcription quality is genuinely impressive - not the hedging "pretty good for AI" kind, but the kind where you scroll back through a dense technical discussion and find it got everything right.

I use Granola every single day and it has become indispensable to my workflow. On mobile, it's perfect for capturing conversations during walks and transcribing meetings on the go. The one-tap capture makes it effortless to start recording without breaking focus.

apps.title: Google NotebookLM
apps.verdict: NotebookLM solves a problem no classic notebook can: you upload your sources and the AI works strictly within them, without making things up. Students, researchers, and professionals with large document sets call it a game-changer. The app lags behind the web version, and you can only download audio through the browser.
apps.loved: The AI only answers from uploaded sources and honestly cites where it pulls information from: hallucinations are minimal. The audio overview feature turns dry documents into a lively podcast you can listen to on a walk. Works with PDFs, videos, and notes simultaneously.
apps.weak: The mobile app does not let you download generated materials: you have to switch to the website. Audio always comes out as a podcast-style dialogue with no option to get a monologue or lecture format. Sharing with people outside the Google ecosystem barely works.
apps.whoFor: Students and researchers who need to quickly absorb a large body of material. Professionals working with a corpus of documents where accuracy and source citations matter.

quotes.text: If you've ever stared at a mountain of PDFs, research papers, meeting notes, or YouTube transcripts and thought, "There has to be a smarter way to make sense of all this," Google NotebookLM is your answer.

apps.title: Noteful: Notes & PDF Markup
apps.verdict: Noteful has a clean interface, smooth writing, and accurate PDF annotation. Most users who switched from major competitors stay. No color picker, no shape alignment.
apps.loved: Writing is smooth, PDF annotation is precise, and the ruler scales correctly when zoomed. No forced AI or bloat: just what you need for notes. One-time purchase with no subscription surprises later.
apps.weak: The color picker does not work correctly. There are no alignment or snapping tools for shapes. Handwritten text search is not available: you cannot find a note by its content.
apps.whoFor: Students and professionals who need a reliable handwritten note-taking and PDF annotation tool without a subscription. Especially suited to those burned by constantly changing terms from major competitors.

quotes.text: No seriously, check the title. I NEVER write reviews. But this one absolutely deserves it. I have tried many note apps and this one is by far the best one. First of all, i bought Goodnotes back in like 2020. Then it turned into a subscription model and I left.

apps.title: My Wonderful Days Journal
apps.verdict: A journal with a one-entry-per-day format. Users keep coming back to it for a decade. Keyword search finds entries from any year. Backup only happens once a month: without a manual backup before a phone reset, you can lose several weeks of entries.
apps.loved: The one-entry-per-date format keeps the habit going: you can see every day you missed. Full-text search finds entries from any year instantly. iCloud sync has worked for years without data loss for most users.
apps.weak: Backup only runs once a month: if your phone resets without a manual backup, you can lose weeks of entries. The interface is small and has not been updated for modern screens. You cannot insert a photo directly into the body of an entry.
apps.whoFor: People who want to journal every day without complex structure and do not need to sync entries across different services.

quotes.text: I did the latest update and all my notes got deleted from the last SEVEN years. If you have backups on in the app you can restore from there. BUT they only backup the first of every month. So I had lost one month of (important) entries.

I don't write reviews usually but—in my opinion, this app deserves some public commendation. TEN YEARS I've been using this app now; I just checked. (Strangely, to the month! So call this my 'decade anniversary' review.) I always just used it simply and relied on it.

I've been using this app since I had an iphone 4! I love it, I can search certain words and it will show me every entry that contained that word. It even does throwbacks, shows you what you wrote on the same day a year ago.
I haven't kept a regular journal in years before MWD. Now it's simple and delightful to write about the good, not-so-good, inspiring and trying events in my life. It's truly a wonderful app.

apps.title: RemNote - Notes & Flashcards
apps.verdict: A note-taking system with built-in spaced repetition: when you create a note, a flashcard for review is created at the same time. The web version and desktop are stable. The mobile app lags behind, with occasional freezes when opening daily notes and sync issues after long desktop sessions. Indispensable for medicine and the hard sciences.
apps.loved: Notes and flashcards are created simultaneously without extra steps. Built-in spaced repetition beats Anki in interface convenience. Sync between the web version and mobile works in most cases.
apps.weak: The mobile app freezes when opening the daily notes section and requires reinstallation. After extended desktop sessions, sync on the phone falls behind.
apps.whoFor: Medical and science students who need to take notes and prepare flashcards for exams at the same time.

quotes.text: I started school again last month, and I was on the hunt for a program that would consolidate my notes all in one place. I am an organizational nut, and I needed a better system. Being an avid fan of Anki already, I somehow stumbled upon this program.

I used to have so many random notes in my notes app, or pages, or some random new app I'd try and delete within a few days and couldn't keep it all straight. I started using this for my foreign language studies because of its flash card feature.

apps.title: Drafts
apps.verdict: The best app for instant thought capture with routing to wherever it needs to go. Opens straight to a blank page, runs instantly, and supports scripts and integrations with dozens of services. A tool for people who already know what they want to automate.
apps.loved: Opens instantly to empty text with no extra taps before you start typing. Actions let you send text to Obsidian, Slack, OmniFocus, or any other service with one tap. Dictation via Apple Watch works reliably.
apps.weak: High learning curve: without reading the documentation, most of the app's capabilities stay hidden. Voice input from the iPhone keyboard sometimes stops after a few words. Advanced automation features are only available in the extended version.
apps.whoFor: Developers, journalists, and power users who need fast capture with automatic routing to other systems.

quotes.text: Drafts is so good! I installed it randomly because it looked interesting and since it was free, it didn't hurt to check it out. Immediately after installing it, I fell in love and upgraded to a paid subscription.

I'm blown away by the power of the app. It's transforming my workflow. I'm constantly wishing that I could do this or that only to discover that it's already baked in or easy to add with a bit of simple scripting. I can't believe how customizable it is.

apps.title: Sticky Notes HD
apps.verdict: A quick notepad for short notes with color-coded sticky notes. A notification-bar widget lets you scroll through notes without opening the app. Sync between iPad and iPhone works. There is no autosave: you have to tap the checkmark or edits are lost.
apps.loved: The widget lets you read notes directly from the notification shade without opening the app. Color-coding for priorities. Alarm-based reminders for urgent tasks.
apps.weak: No autosave: edits disappear if you do not tap the confirm button. No folders for grouping sticky notes by topic.
apps.whoFor: People who want to keep a few current reminders always within reach in a widget and do not need long structured notes.

quotes.text: After spending several hours test driving various sticky note apps, I frankly gave up the notion of ever finding one to my liking. The ones I tried were too time consuming in respect to navigation, they would delete notes on their own, they were not very well laid out

Apple needs to fly Mr. Tsopanakis to Cupertino and woo him with royalty payments or a briefcase full of stock options. Then, Sticky Notes HD needs to be standard in every iOS release. Sticky Notes HD is the definition of serenity.

apps.title: Notesnook: Private note taking
apps.verdict: An open-source encrypted organizer: end-to-end encryption, cross-platform support, nested notebooks, and tags. A growing alternative for users who care about data privacy.
apps.loved: End-to-end encryption with full functionality intact. Reliable cross-platform sync between Windows, Linux, and iPhone. Note history and the ability to publish a note via a link.
apps.weak: Occasional outages with no sync access: several users reported sync being unavailable for multiple days in a row. A few users lost notes after their extended subscription ended. Navigation between sections is inconsistent.
apps.whoFor: Privacy-conscious users and former Evernote subscribers looking for a cross-platform replacement.

quotes.text: I used to love Evernote, but they got way too expensive and they violated the trust of their customer base. For those who want to support an app that respects the right to privacy while offering a feature-rich note-taking app, Notesnook is the clear answer.

I've been looking for a notes app for a long time that scratches the itch I have to keep things synced and organized. I moved from Google Keep which was OK but was missing some serious organization and power.

apps.title: Todoist: To Do List & Calendar
apps.verdict: One of the most thoughtfully designed task managers in the sample: natural language for date input, instant capture via widget or voice, and smooth performance across all platforms. People with ADHD and cognitive differences call it a lifesaver. The weakest point: the Google Calendar integration lost two-way sync.
apps.loved: A task can be added in seconds from anywhere: widget, voice, or quick entry with date recognition. Long-term users trust it as the single home for all their commitments: nothing gets lost or forgotten. Recurring tasks and projects are configured flexibly.
apps.weak: The Google Calendar integration lost two-way sync after a redesign: tasks from projects do not appear there. Deleting a project destroys all tasks inside it without warning and with no way to recover them. On mobile, recurring reminders are not displayed.
apps.whoFor: People with busy lives who need to offload everything from their head into one place and stop holding things mentally. Especially valued by those with ADHD or irregular schedules.

quotes.text: I've been using Todoist for at least seven years now and I have it well integrated into my daily life. It is the one place I can throw anything at any time and not have to think about it again. Wake up at 3am with a thought, add it and I know it's taken care of.

apps.title: Bear - Markdown Notes
apps.verdict: The best plain-text Markdown note-taking tool in the sample. Opens instantly, and the tag system replaces folders while working more flexibly. iCloud sync is reliable. Bear 2.0 removed the convenient toolbar, worsening the iPhone experience.
apps.loved: The tag system lets you find a note across multiple intersecting topics without creating folders. Works equally fast on iPhone and Mac, and iCloud sync requires no separate account. Markdown renders beautifully without getting in the way while typing.
apps.weak: Bear 2.0 removed the compact toolbar: formatting is now awkward on a small screen. Search does not support advanced filters and is slow in large archives. Attachments and PDFs are not supported without the premium subscription.
apps.whoFor: Writers, developers, and researchers who need a fast Markdown editor with reliable sync across the Apple ecosystem.

quotes.text: UPDATE: I've had this app for a few years now and still use it DAILY. I've looked at a couple other notes apps at times, just out of curiosity when I see them, but none have come close. I haven't needed to use a single other notes-like app since I switched to Bear.

Bear was absolutely perfect before the 2.0 update. There was a very slim/narrow bar along the top of the keyboard with all the functions. You had to slide it to get to some of them, but after 30 minutes' use, it wasn't a big deal. Plus it was FAST.

The first time I tried this app I got overwhelmed, it felt like the tags were fussy and I wasn't sure how to organize stuff. This was when I first got apple products and was seeking a notes app. Then I slowly worked my way through all the features.

apps.title: Inkflow Plus Visual Notebook
apps.verdict: A freeform notebook with flexible layout: text, drawing, and photos on the same page, a selection tool for moving elements, and export to image and document formats. A favorite tool of architects, educators, and anyone the standard text editor feels too confined for.
apps.loved: Free placement of text blocks and drawings on a single page with no grid. A selection tool for capturing and moving fragments. Stable operation for many years with no data loss.
apps.weak: No cloud sync between devices. The learning curve for new users is noticeable and not all features are obvious. The price of the premium version gives some users pause.
apps.whoFor: Designers, educators, and systems architects who need to mix handwriting, diagrams, and photos in one space.

quotes.text: There are a few good apps that are devoted exclusively to handwriting -- that is, they do not also include a capability for typing. Because their use requires a minimum of set-up activity, these are the apps that you grab when you need to just get something down.

apps.title: Feenote - Notes and lists
apps.verdict: A feature-rich notebook with folders, handwriting input, and formatting. Students praise it for usability on older iPads. Handwriting via finger is only available during a trial period, and several students lost important notes.
apps.loved: Rich selection of fonts and formatting in the free version. Works well for taking notes on older iPads that other apps do not support. Folders and organization by topic.
apps.weak: Handwriting via finger or stylus is only available in the premium version after a short trial. Several students lost important notes while working in the app. PDF export cannot be edited.
apps.whoFor: Students and schoolchildren who take notes on an iPad and want a free GoodNotes alternative with standard note organization features.

apps.title: mimi – Cute notes
apps.verdict: A beautiful notebook with design customization: themes, fonts, stickers, and pastel backgrounds. Works without registration. Notes are stored on-device only: no cloud backup, and everything is gone if the app is deleted.
apps.loved: A large library of themes and fonts without forcing you into a subscription. An interface free of intrusive interruptions during use. Separate password-protected notebooks let you keep private notes alongside general ones.
apps.weak: Notes are stored on-device only: delete the app or break your phone and everything is gone. No cloud backup or cross-device sync. Some themes move a note to the top of the list every time it is edited.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers and young adults who care about a beautiful journal interface and are not worried about long-term storage.

quotes.text: Though it looks like a cute notes app (the reason I bought it as well) do not buy it. It DOES NOT save any of your notes even with a subscription, so it's very easy to use all your notes like I did. I had so much on this app, but it is NOT worth it.

I love this note app so much, I use it as my main notes app. The customization is amazing, and it’s very cute. So many fonts, backgrounds, font sizes, bold, underline, colors etc. It’s really useful and visually pleasing too. I hope the dev

apps.title: Notebooks: Write and Organize
apps.verdict: A deep organizer with nested folders, Markdown support, WebDAV and Dropbox sync, and multi-format export. A longtime favorite for those who want to own their data without a forced cloud subscription.
apps.loved: Reliable sync via WebDAV and Dropbox, unlimited folder hierarchy, and stable operation over many years. Does not break during updates.
apps.weak: Dropbox dependency limits users with three or more devices. Some features (drawing, Fountain) are advertised but work unreliably. Migrating from older versions of the app caused document loss for some users.
apps.whoFor: Writers and researchers who need a long-term, reliable knowledge base with a folder structure and no cloud subscription.

quotes.text: TLDR; If you have been looking for a notebook app that is not a subscription with portable data and deeply integrated in the apple ecosystem system, this is it. I looked a long time at different note apps. I would not have found this if I hadn't been so particular.

apps.title: Daily Journal: Diary with Lock
apps.verdict: A personal journal with a PIN code, mood tracker, and entry templates. The screen blurs when you switch apps. Transferring entries on a phone upgrade is unreliable.
apps.loved: PIN and Face ID locking with automatic blur when leaving the app. A mood tracker with a timestamp on every entry. Templates help you start writing when you do not know where to begin.
apps.weak: Transferring entries to a new phone is unreliable: several users lost their history. Screen orientation is locked to portrait, which is awkward on a tablet. Some features are unavailable without the premium version, and the reasons for the split are not explained.
apps.whoFor: People who want a private protected journal space on a single device, especially those who live with curious family members. Not suited for long-term storage with data migration.

apps.title: Spelling Notebook: Learn, Test
apps.verdict: A specialized spelling trainer: you create a word list and the app reads the words aloud and accepts your typed answer. The built-in dictionary with speech synthesis covers most needs. The 8-word limit per list in the free version is a problem for older students.
apps.loved: Built-in speech synthesis pronounces words without needing a parent to record audio. You can add your own words with custom pronunciation. Progress history lets you track improvement over time.
apps.weak: The free version is limited to eight words per list: not enough for older students or spelling competition participants. Word lists cannot be shared between different users' devices. In test mode the word is visible on screen, which reduces training effectiveness.
apps.whoFor: Parents who want children to practice spelling independently without adult dictation, and participants in spelling competitions.

apps.title: TwinMind - AI Notes & Memory
apps.verdict: A transcription tool for meetings and voice notes with automatic summaries and contextual search across your full history. Valued by students and professionals with packed meeting schedules. Recording sometimes silently cuts out mid-meeting.
apps.loved: Instant summaries of hour-long meetings, contextual search across all past recordings, background operation while another app is open. Transcription is faster than most alternatives.
apps.weak: Recording sometimes silently stops mid-meeting without warning, losing part of the conversation. No tags or folders to organize accumulated recordings. The app occasionally freezes, putting the safety of the recording in doubt.
apps.whoFor: Professionals with dense meeting schedules and students who need to capture what is said without manual note-taking.

apps.title: Taio - Markdown & Text Actions
apps.verdict: A powerful Markdown editor with an action system for automating text operations, iCloud support, and Obsidian compatibility. Long in active development, but over the past year updates have nearly stopped, which worries regular users.
apps.loved: The action system lets you automate any text operation. Fast iCloud sync. Excellent accessibility for screen reader users.
apps.weak: Development has effectively been frozen for over a year. No Dropbox support as a primary storage option. Sync sometimes fails to detect local changes and suggests conflict merges.
apps.whoFor: Developers and technical writers working in the Obsidian or plain-text ecosystem who need a mobile editor with automation.

quotes.text: Adding to the review below. Export no longer works. Adding to the review below. There's nothing more irritating in markdown editors than auto-numbering that then fails.

My favorite way to take typed notes on my Mac is with the Obsidian app, but that app lacks a mobile counterpart; this is where Taio comes in. With Taio, I can edit the markdown files that I create in Obsidian by taking advantage of its iCloud integration.

apps.title: Obsidian - Connected Notes
apps.verdict: A powerful linked-note system in Markdown format with files stored on-device. The desktop version is strong. The mobile version falls short: text input is awkward, the cursor jumps, and iCloud sync is unreliable.
apps.loved: Full ownership of data as plain text files. A graph of connections between notes for navigating the knowledge base. A massive plugin ecosystem. Works offline.
apps.weak: Mobile text input is uncomfortable: the cursor jumps during manual editing and the toolbar disappears. iCloud sync causes a black screen and missing vaults for some users. High barrier to entry: the app is not for anyone unfamiliar with Markdown.
apps.whoFor: Researchers, programmers, and writers building a long-term knowledge base on desktop who use the phone only for reading and quick edits.

quotes.text: Obsidian is a great editing platform. Very extensible and customizable, and I enjoy it a lot. I like that it's OSS, and that my data is encrypted and stored in plaintext.

The vast majority of note apps I've tried do almost nothing to actually take advantage of being digital notes. They give folders and pages of notes you make and thats it. God forbid we ever innovate past emulating paper notes in a binder for digital notes.

Maybe it's just the way our brains age, but I'm a 40yo well-educated professional in technology and education and this app is incredibly intimidating. If you don't already work in markdown this may not be the best place to start.

apps.title: Paper: Writing App, Notes
apps.verdict: A minimalist editor for long-form writing with beautiful typography and a focus mode. The developer responds to reviews promptly. Several users lost all their documents without warning.
apps.loved: A clean interface with no extraneous elements gives the feeling of writing on paper. A good selection of fonts. The developer responds to feedback and fixes bugs promptly.
apps.weak: Several users lost all their documents with no way to recover them. Font changes and toolbar customization are only available in the premium version. The built-in AI pushes itself forward with no way to fully disable it from the interface.
apps.whoFor: Authors of long-form writing who value a distraction-free interface and work primarily with short to medium-length texts.

apps.title: Werdsmith: Writing App
apps.verdict: An app for long-form texts and books, not for quick notes. Helps structure a manuscript: ideas separate, chapters separate, word count built in. Not suited for on-the-go capture: no widget, no quick capture.
apps.loved: Daily and total word count statistics motivate consistent writing. The project-and-ideas structure lets you keep a draft and notes side by side without mixing them. Ghostwriter can continue your text without breaking your style.
apps.weak: Large manuscripts of 80,000+ words start showing noticeable lag. There is no quick thought capture: creating a note requires going through several screens. No widget and no integrations with other tools.
apps.whoFor: Authors working on long-form texts: novels, screenplays, campaigns. Not designed for everyday notes.

apps.title: Inkpad Notepad - Notes - To do
apps.verdict: A simple cross-platform notepad that has existed for over a decade and has not lost data for most users in that time. Sync via its own account works between Android and iOS. In the past year or two, complaints about a grey screen on launch have appeared, fixed by reinstalling. No frills, but it reliably holds text notes and lists.
apps.loved: Sync works between Android and iPhone without data loss when switching devices: several authors confirm this over a 10-year horizon. Opens quickly, easy to find the note you need from the list.
apps.weak: Recent updates bring a grey launch screen that only clears with a reinstall. Several users reported complete note loss after cloud sync. Search within notes is absent or weak.
apps.whoFor: People who need a reliable text notepad for long lists and notes with no extra features.

apps.title: Inkflow Visual Notebook
apps.verdict: A freeform drawing and handwriting notepad where any element can be selected, moved, and scaled. The key strength is a lasso tool for reorganizing page content. No eraser in the traditional sense, only undo. Not suited for iPhone and optimized for iPad.
apps.loved: A selection tool for free scaling of any element on the page. Smooth input by finger or stylus with no lag. PDF export.
apps.weak: No eraser: only undo through the history. Switching colors and tools requires extra steps. On iPhone the functionality is significantly cut back.
apps.whoFor: People who make visual notes, mind maps, and sketches on iPad and want to freely reorganize page content after writing.

apps.title: My Diary - Journal with Lock
apps.verdict: A beautiful journal with a lock, swappable themes, stickers, and a mood tracker. People who start writing in it come back for years. The main flaw: when switching devices or deleting the app, several users lost years of entries.
apps.loved: Changing themes and decorations motivates returning to the journal every day. The password lock carries over when switching between Android and iOS. A mood tracker with a graph over time helps spot patterns in how you feel.
apps.weak: Data export is unreliable: when moving to another device or after deleting the app, some users lost all entries permanently. The app does not always save the latest edits correctly when closed. Sync between iOS and Android only works in one direction.
apps.whoFor: People who want a beautiful personal space for daily journaling or mood tracking. Regular manual backups are important.

apps.title: abcNotes Full Version
apps.verdict: A sticky-note board with multiple desktops, Mac sync, and flexible background and font customization. Long-term users value it for its practicality, but data loss during major updates is a recurring story.
apps.loved: Multiple named desktops for different topics, custom photo backgrounds, and sync with the desktop app for those who set it up.
apps.weak: Several users lost all their notes after an app update. Sync often fails to detect deleted notes on other devices. Managing checkboxes in lists is awkward.
apps.whoFor: Organized Apple ecosystem users who want visual sticky notes synced across iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

apps.title: Element Note
apps.verdict: A handwriting app for iPad with Apple Pencil. Pen stabilization and writing quality are better than GoodNotes. Several major updates broke existing notes by retroactively changing how tools looked.
apps.loved: Pen stabilization produces the most beautiful handwriting among comparable apps. A clean interface with no extra buttons. Diverse pen options: calligraphy, pencil, marker.
apps.weak: Major updates broke existing notes several times by retroactively changing tool appearance. Several users lost all data after the app froze. The developer was slow to respond to reports of serious problems.
apps.whoFor: iPad students who take handwritten notes and want beautiful writing without a GoodNotes subscription.

apps.title: WeNote - Notes, Notepad, To do
apps.verdict: A color-coded notepad with tabs: fast, intuitive, with reminders and categories. Good for everyday lists. Cross-device sync is locked behind the premium version.
apps.loved: The color category system makes chaos manageable at a glance. Several users report years of use with no data loss.
apps.weak: Several cases of complete note loss after updates. Cross-device sync is only available in the premium version. Reminders are unreliable.
apps.whoFor: Android users who switched to iPhone and were used to ColorNote, and anyone who wants a simple color-coded organizer for everyday lists.

apps.title: Mininote - Cute note and diary
apps.verdict: A customizable journal with a huge selection of stickers, backgrounds, and fonts, plus a tool for cutting stickers from photos. Keeps users engaged through creative decoration. Freezes when the sticker gallery opens, and some users' pages disappeared.
apps.loved: A sticker-cutting tool that works with any photo and the ability to publish your own templates for other users. A huge library of backgrounds and fonts. The app inspires regular journaling through its aesthetics.
apps.weak: The app freezes when the sticker gallery is opened and sometimes crashes at the start of a session. Several users lost pages due to a network error with no autosave. The password recovery interface does not work correctly: switching accounts does not restore previous settings.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers and young adults who care about beautiful, creative personal journal design. Not for business notes or long-term storage of important data.

apps.title: Notebook - Diary & Journal App
apps.verdict: A simple journal with a chronological structure that does not lose entries for most users. Several people have used it for 10 or more years. No text formatting, no iPad support.
apps.loved: Chronological navigation by page-turning creates the feel of a real journal. Date search works, and an entry's creation date never changes. Several users have kept it for more than 10 years without data loss.
apps.weak: No text formatting: no bold, italic, or font size options. No iPad support: the app is optimized only for iPhone. Some users report incorrect page-turning behavior on long entries.
apps.whoFor: People who want a simple, durable personal text-only journal with no extra features. Especially suited to those who value chronological navigation.

apps.title: Ulysses: Writing App
apps.verdict: A professional environment for long-form writing: novels, articles, dissertations. A unified library with instant search and reliable sync between Mac, iPad, and iPhone. Markdown symbols are always visible during editing with no way to switch to clean text mode.
apps.loved: A single library of all texts with instant content search. Cross-device sync works reliably. Export to PDF, DOCX, and WordPress publishing from one place.
apps.weak: Markdown symbols are always visible during editing: there is no clean text mode for comfortable typing. Sync for some users has started failing, losing edits without warning. Grammar checking is tuned for formal academic style and gets in the way when writing fiction.
apps.whoFor: Authors of long-form texts on the Apple ecosystem who need a unified manuscript library with reliable sync between Mac and iPad.

quotes.text: Ulysses ranks at the top end of professional writing programs. Among it's outstanding features are the all-in-one Library. Everything you've ever written (if you like), plus everything you are currently working on or ever will work on, is accessible from one window.

apps.title: Notepad: Easy Notes & Memos
apps.verdict: A simple and fast notepad that handles everyday lists and short notes well. Users value the speed and clean look. Several people report losing all data after an update, and a change to date logic in an update frustrated long-term users.
apps.loved: Opens and is ready to type faster than most competitors. A clean, readable interface without clutter. Works across multiple devices without extra setup.
apps.weak: Several users lost all accumulated notes after an app update. One update changed the modification date when simply opening a note, breaking the sort order for long-term users. Formatting and attachments are absent, which limits use cases.
apps.whoFor: People who want a digital notepad strictly for short notes and lists with no extra features. Not for long-term storage of important data.

apps.title: Notebook – Notes, Notepad
apps.verdict: A Zoho app with custom notebook covers and cross-platform sync. Cover customization and formatting work. Notes periodically disappear, partially or fully, for different users.
apps.loved: Custom notebook covers with any photo create a personal feel. Cross-platform support works between iOS and Android without extra steps. Rich text formatting options available in the free version.
apps.weak: Content periodically disappears partially or fully: the problem recurs across different users. The interface freezes during navigation, with some users hitting dead ends and unexpected crashes. The company introduced storage limits for existing users without warning.
apps.whoFor: Users who care about visual organization through different notebooks with covers and need iOS and Android cross-platform support. Regular manual backups are recommended.

apps.title: HyNote: AI Note Taker, Summary
apps.verdict: A transcription and summarization tool with extra features: YouTube note-taking, test generation, and podcast-style playback of your notes. Works best for students with ADHD who need multiple formats of the same material. Key problem is opaque limits. Even on expensive tiers there is a monthly minute cap that is never disclosed upfront. Instability at critical moments is a proven pattern.
apps.loved: Generates a quiz from a lecture in seconds, letting you check comprehension immediately after class. Summarizes YouTube videos directly from a link without downloading. Voice lecture recording and automatic notes work together.
apps.weak: Even on expensive tiers there is a monthly transcription cap that is nowhere clearly stated before you hit it. The app breaks during important meetings without warning. Transcription is unreliable for long lectures on iPad.
apps.whoFor: Students with ADHD or dyslexia who need to reformat lectures into notes and quizzes with one tap.

quotes.text: As the title already states, I have ADHD and Autism. I have a difficult time with note taking because I oftentimes want to write EVERYTHING down rather than key points. As you can imagine, this makes it difficult to stay focused on the actual topic.

apps.title: Notepad - handy quickly memo
apps.verdict: A simple notepad for quick notes: opens instantly and lets you start typing without intermediate screens. Several users lost all data after an update with no way to recover it.
apps.loved: Opens instantly and lets you start typing without intermediate screens. A few notes with color coding and simple folders are enough for most everyday needs. Works without a required account.
apps.weak: Several users lost all data after an app update with no way to recover it. No text formatting: bold, headings, and lists are unavailable. No content search within notes.
apps.whoFor: People who want a digital scrap of paper for notes and lists with no settings or registration. Not suited for long-term storage of valuable data.

quotes.text: Alright, I've been trying different Note apps and for sure I have to say this is the best one I've used. It's simple to use and very quick to access and all.

apps.title: MyNotePad
apps.verdict: A simple notepad with font and paper color choices as a replacement for the default Apple Notes app. Works offline with no cross-device sync. The app is not being updated and is periodically incompatible with new iOS versions. Several users lost fragments of notes with no apparent cause.
apps.loved: Font selection creates the feel of a real notebook. Simple note navigation via a sidebar. Autosave on close.
apps.weak: No cross-device sync. Several users reported losing fragments of note content with no updates to blame. The app is outdated and does not support current iOS versions.
apps.whoFor: People looking for a simple offline notepad on a single device with a slightly nicer font than the default Apple app.

apps.title: Post-it®
apps.verdict: A digital version of sticky notes that 3M has made surprisingly useful. Visual boards, note grouping, and scanning paper sticky notes all work well. Reliability is shaky: several users' notes disappeared without warning. Text editing is unintuitive and sync sometimes breaks. Strong where visual organization is needed rather than linear text.
apps.loved: Scanning paper sticky notes into digital format works instantly. Visual boards with grouping and resizable cards help structure projects. The home screen widget updates in real time.
apps.weak: Notes sometimes disappear by entire boards with no way to recover them. Text editing is unclear and awkward. Cross-device sync breaks periodically.
apps.whoFor: Visual thinkers who are used to thinking in sticky notes and teams moving physical boards to their phones.

apps.title: 국민 메모장 솜노트 - SomNote
apps.verdict: A notepad with a folder structure, color themes, and cloud sync. Long-term users praise it for simplicity and organization.
apps.loved: A folder hierarchy for different areas of life, fast keyword search, and an automatic date stamp on every entry.
apps.weak: Sync is slow and sometimes hangs. The text editor lacks bold, italic, and alignment options.
apps.whoFor: Users who need a simple folder-based notepad for tracking several parallel topics: a journal, recipes, work notes.

apps.title: Prayer Notebook
apps.verdict: A specialized planner for prayer practices with a schedule, categories, and a card mode. The interface is simple and unobtrusive. Central problem: sync between iPhone and iPad does not work despite being advertised. Some users bought both versions separately for a feature that never worked.
apps.loved: A card mode where prayer requests scroll by one at a time without the distraction of the full list. The ability to assign days of the week and individual reminders to each entry is cited as the main differentiator from competitors.
apps.weak: Sync between devices does not work: documented in dozens of reviews over several years. Entry creation dates are not shown, making it hard to track history. Text in cards is cut off with no line wrapping.
apps.whoFor: People who keep a structured prayer journal on a single device and do not expect to switch between iPhone and iPad.

apps.title: Notepad Sanrio characters
apps.verdict: A desktop widget notepad featuring Sanrio characters. Lets you keep one note visible directly on your phone screen. Limitation: only one note at a time, and the background color does not show in the widget.
apps.loved: A widget with favorite characters always in view. Daily spins of a capsule machine to unlock new designs. No forced content size limits.
apps.weak: Only one note for the whole app: you cannot keep separate reminders for different tasks. Background color and decoration settings do not appear in the home screen widget. Maximum note length is 1000 characters.
apps.whoFor: Sanrio fans who want one visible reminder note on their phone screen with cute styling.

apps.title: DAYOL: Journal, Calendar
apps.verdict: An aesthetically pleasing digital journal with stickers, custom covers, and calendar integration. A favorite among people who keep personal journals. Entries become inaccessible after updates, and text scrolls down forcibly while typing.
apps.loved: A huge sticker library and custom page covers. New decor can be earned by watching short videos without a mandatory purchase. Calendar integration for planning directly in the journal.
apps.weak: Entries disappear or become inaccessible after updates. Text scrolls down forcibly while typing, making it impossible to see what you are writing. Image insertion without compression does not work.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers and young adults for whom the aesthetics of a personal journal with decorations and customization matter more than reliable storage.

quotes.text: I have had this app since late 2024 and it efficiently gets the job done. The numerous stickers are so cute and the text colors are so versatile, allowing me to add life to my diary entries.

apps.title: Paintwork - Infinite Notebook
apps.verdict: A drawing app with an infinite canvas and symmetry mode. A solid starting point for those looking for a drawing app with axis symmetry. After updates, the fill bucket stopped working correctly and unsaved data is lost when the app freezes.
apps.loved: The symmetry function with a configurable number of axes is available in the free version. An infinite canvas does not limit work size. Works without registration: download and draw.
apps.weak: After some updates the fill bucket stopped working correctly: it fills the whole canvas instead of a shape. The app freezes when using the symmetry tool, and unsaved data is lost. Controls are small and awkward on a small screen.
apps.whoFor: Beginning artists and children who need a free digital sketching tool without a subscription. Professionals and serious project users should look elsewhere.

apps.title: Google Keep - Notes and lists
apps.verdict: Google Keep wins on instant capture: sticky note, list, voice memo in one tap. Works well for short, disposable reminders. But search misses content and is slow, label-based organization is primitive, and some users' notes periodically disappear or fail to sync between devices.
apps.loved: Voice memos with automatic transcription directly in the interface. Instant capture via a lock screen widget. Integration with other Google services works without extra setup.
apps.weak: Search misses note content and runs with a delay. Structure is only through color labels: no nesting or folders, and with many notes things turn to chaos. Several users report notes periodically disappearing without explanation.
apps.whoFor: Google ecosystem users who need to quickly catch a thought or make a list and are fine forgetting about it within a week. Not the best choice for long-term storage of important notes.

quotes.text: I really want to like Google Keep because the concept is great, but using it on iOS has been incredibly frustrating. The biggest issue is the keyboard behavior. Whenever I'm editing a note, if I stop typing for about 5 seconds, the keyboard dismisses itself.

apps.title: tatter
apps.verdict: A sticky-note board for visual thinkers: color cards on a cork wall, easy repositioning and resizing. The core works well, but the app has broken navigation several times after updates, and while most users appreciate the simplicity, reliability of storage raises real concerns.
apps.loved: Instant card creation with no extra steps, visual spatial arrangement of notes, colors and simplicity. Exactly what list-based apps lack.
apps.weak: Notes disappear after updates with no way to recover them. Navigation between pages has changed for the worse several times. No cross-device sync.
apps.whoFor: Visual thinkers who need a digital cork board for quick ideas, lists, and reminders on one screen.

quotes.text: So I wrote a review a little while back praising this app. It used to function simply and perfectly. I used to have a board that I could add notes to, the notes would all be the same size, and I could flip to the next page. Now it's all different and clunky.

apps.title: Colored Note
apps.verdict: A simple color-coded notepad with mood selection. Stable for years, but a series of updates broke manual sorting. Data disappeared for several users after updates with no way to recover it.
apps.loved: Color-coded notes and speed. Mood selection when creating an entry is cited by several users as an unexpectedly useful detail.
apps.weak: Notes disappear after updates: documented by multiple users with years of history. Manual sorting was removed in one update without warning. No cross-device sync, and accidental deletion happens without a confirmation prompt or undo.
apps.whoFor: People who want a color-coded organizer for short notes on a single device and are willing to accept the risk of data loss during updates.

quotes.text: I've used this app for years. Since 2015, actually. But over the last couple of months it has become very difficult to use. And it is not the phone because I've changed phones but the app keeps not working.

apps.title: CollaNote: Notes & PDF Markup
apps.verdict: CollaNote with a generous handwriting toolkit and PDF annotation. A series of updates introduced a page limit without warning and added bugs to basic features. Students who had used the app for years found themselves with restricted access in the middle of an academic semester.
apps.loved: Smooth writing with Apple Pencil and a wide toolset in the free version. The developer historically responded quickly to user requests. PDF annotation with import worked reliably before recent updates.
apps.weak: A 10-page limit was introduced without warning: users discovered it mid-semester. Annotations on PDFs shift position when the file is reopened. Voice translation switches on by itself even after being disabled in settings.
apps.whoFor: Students willing to keep an eye on changing terms and pay for premium if the app stabilizes. Currently a risk for those who depend on it daily.

quotes.text: I've been using CollaNote for over three years now, and I initially chose it because of its great free features compared to paid apps like GoodNotes and Notability. It offered excellent functionality without forcing users to subscribe, which was a breath of fresh air.

apps.title: Sticky Notes - MemoCool Notepad
apps.verdict: A gamified sticky-note notepad with a fridge instead of a board: magnets, background changes, and mini-games for earning coins. Makes note-keeping fun, but data is tied to the device and is lost when switching phones without account migration.
apps.loved: The game-like atmosphere makes daily notes enjoyable. Earned coins unlock new magnets and themes without real spending.
apps.weak: Data does not migrate between phones through an account: several users lost everything when switching devices. No screen rotation on tablet. No cross-device sync.
apps.whoFor: Users who want to make note-taking enjoyable and game-like without needing serious storage for important data.

apps.title: Penbook: Paper Planner & Notes
apps.verdict: A beautiful app for handwritten journals with pen pressure that beats most competitors. Stability lets it down: pages disappear when working with stickers and photos, and iCloud sync is unreliable.
apps.loved: The pen reproduces pressure more accurately than most competitors, creating the feel of real paper. Templates for engineering tasks, bullet journaling, and habit trackers are all in one place. Navigation between journals is intuitive after a short learning period.
apps.weak: iCloud sync is unpredictable: entries appear and disappear after switching devices. The app freezes when working with stickers and photos, sometimes erasing entire pages. After updates, some users lost all data with no way to recover it.
apps.whoFor: People who want a beautiful digital journal for personal writing and are not storing critically important data there.

apps.title: Journey - Diary, Journal
apps.verdict: A cross-platform journal with a web version, geotagging, photos, and search. One of the few where you can open entries from a browser. Several users lost years of entries after updates with no recovery available.
apps.loved: Cross-platform support (Android, iOS, Mac, web) with sync that works under normal conditions. An 'on this day' feature and the ability to attach photos, videos, and a geotag to each entry.
apps.weak: Several users lost years of entries after updates with no way to recover them. Support responds with a week or more of delay. When the premium subscription ends, some features stop working.
apps.whoFor: People who journal across multiple devices and want browser access. Manual export backups are critical: do not count on the built-in backup.

quotes.text: UPDATE. I really loved this app. I purchased a one-year membership after enjoying it for about six months. I did not renew as money was tight. Everything I had written since the beginning disappeared. I am so sad. About 18 months worth of entries.

apps.title: StickyNote: Home Screen Notes
apps.verdict: A widget app for color-coded sticky notes on the lock screen and home screen. Simple and attractive, but basic text formatting is absent, help is only available in Japanese, and the widget periodically stops displaying.
apps.loved: Color-coded widgets with sticky notes on the lock screen or home screen are instantly visible without opening the app. Rich background options.
apps.weak: No text formatting inside a note: only one font and one size for the whole card. Instructions and help are in Japanese only. The widget stops updating after some system updates.
apps.whoFor: Users who need one or two visible reminders right on their phone screen without complex structure.

quotes.text: I love this app. I post positive quotes and Bible verses on my phone and can see them as soon as I unlock my screen. I do have two requests. 1. You can select a portion of your note to become the widget.

apps.title: Sticky Notes & Color Widget
apps.verdict: Sticky notes on the home screen with color and font customization. The widget periodically stops updating and shows stale data. No note search.
apps.loved: A color-coded home screen widget showing multiple notes at once: that is the main reason people download it. Colors and fonts can be customized in the free version without extra restrictions.
apps.weak: The widget stops updating and shows stale data. The only fix is reinstalling. No note search. Reminder notifications cannot be turned off separately from useful reminders.
apps.whoFor: People who need one or two reminders on their home screen and are willing to pay a subscription for that feature.

quotes.text: This app was wonderful for about a month. But about 2-3 weeks ago it stopped working from the widget. When I want the big widget, it used to be that up to 9 notes would be visible.

apps.title: Microsoft OneNote
apps.verdict: Once a benchmark multi-platform tool, it has degraded: sync breaks regularly, search does not show progress, and the mobile version is generations behind the desktop. People with 10-20 years of history write that their patience has run out.
apps.loved: The notebook-section-page hierarchy lets you store years of varied material in one place. Real-time collaborative editing works without friction. Switching between handwriting and typed text on the same page is rare and valued.
apps.weak: Sync hangs and conflicts: users lose recent edits and are forced to resolve collisions manually. Search does not index parts of content and shows no progress indicator. On Mac the app is effectively non-functional for a noticeable portion of users.
apps.whoFor: Microsoft 365 ecosystem users who need a shared knowledge base with colleagues on Windows. A solo user on Apple devices is better off looking elsewhere.

quotes.text: OneNote is phenomenal on my phone and Windows desktop. I use it all the time. The problem is I also have a Mac laptop. OneNote used to work on the Mac, but now is unusable on the Mac because it does not reliably save changes. This means I can't trust it anymore.

apps.title: Secure Notepad Pro
apps.verdict: A simple password-protected notepad for storing passwords and personal notes. It does one thing: locks notes behind a password. No cross-device sync, no formatting, notes stay on a single phone. Some users lost data after updates.
apps.loved: Instant access without extra steps, reliable password lock, and alphabetical and chronological note sorting.
apps.weak: No cross-device sync: switching phones means losing your data. Several users reported notes disappearing after updates with no way to recover them.
apps.whoFor: People who store passwords and personal data on a single device and do not plan to switch to another phone.

apps.title: Flow: Note Taking & Sketchbook
apps.verdict: A beautiful drawing and handwriting app for iPad with an analog feel for pen pressure. The eraser freezes and fails to erase until the app is restarted. Pages periodically disappear. Needs greater stability for serious work.
apps.loved: The feel of analog tools is reproduced more accurately than in most competitors. An infinite canvas with no page breaks is convenient for diagrams and maps. Quick switching of custom pens via a side panel.
apps.weak: The eraser freezes and does not erase until the app is restarted. Pages sometimes disappear and only reappear when switching from another device. Cross-device sync between iPhone and iPad has failed for several users.
apps.whoFor: Artists and math teachers on iPad Pro with Apple Pencil who are willing to pay a subscription and tolerate instability.

quotes.text: Beautiful app. Writes beautifully as well. But practically speaking, I could not use this for serious note taking. I take pages and pages of notes on a regular basis. That means I need a way to scroll through past notes efficiently.

apps.title: Noteshelf 3: AI Digital Notes
apps.verdict: A handwriting app with Apple Pencil featuring a rich template set and smooth writing. Upgrading from Noteshelf 2 was a disaster for part of the audience: inaccessible notes, lost scanned pages, and broken export. New users without migration baggage are more often satisfied, but instability persists even for them.
apps.loved: Pencil writing quality is called the best among competitors: smoother than GoodNotes. Linked schedules and a wide choice of covers and templates are praised by regular users.
apps.weak: Migration from the previous version breaks access to old notes and loses scanned pages. Export is unreliable. Several users lost important work documents with no way to recover them. The floating toolbar gets in the way of writing.
apps.whoFor: People starting fresh who want a beautiful handwritten journal on iPad. Migrating from Noteshelf 2 is risky without backing up all content first.

apps.title: Freenotes®: AI Notes Taking
apps.verdict: Handwriting converts to text faster and more accurately than most competitors, and the iPad does not overheat during extended sessions. Several users lost all data after an update and iCloud recovery did not work.
apps.loved: Handwriting-to-text conversion works faster and more accurately than most competitors. The interface does not overheat the iPad even during multi-hour sessions. Page and cover customization is broader than the market average.
apps.weak: Data disappears: several users lost all notes after an update with no recovery via iCloud. A splash screen on every launch is annoying. Template tools are more limited than they used to be.
apps.whoFor: Students willing to pay for a lifetime license for smooth handwriting input on iPad. Those who value data storage reliability should look at other options.

apps.title: Secure Notepad
apps.verdict: A simple password-locked notepad that solves one task: keeping notes away from prying eyes. The basic functionality works. But notes are stored locally only with no cloud backup: switching phones means losing everything. A vulnerability via Apple devices allows bypassing the password. Reliability as a storage tool raises serious concerns.
apps.loved: A password at entry plus a security question provide a basic layer of privacy without extra setup. Minimalist interface, works without registration.
apps.weak: Data is stored on-device only: reinstalling or switching phones loses everything. Several users reported complete note loss. Content search barely works.
apps.whoFor: People who want to hide a couple of notes from family members but are not storing anything valuable.

apps.title: Notepad - Simple Notes & Memo
apps.verdict: An ultra-simple notepad with no formatting, no cloud, and no sync. Opens instantly and stays out of the way while you type. Main limitation: notes are stored on-device only. Switching phones means losing everything. Several users report notes vanishing without any apparent reason.
apps.loved: Speed of opening and absence of visual noise: people appreciate that the app does not try to be smarter than the user. Color category tagging and a lock screen widget are mentioned regularly.
apps.weak: Notes do not sync between devices and cannot be recovered after a phone change. Several users lost data without warning. Autocorrect is aggressive and makes mistakes on correctly spelled words.
apps.whoFor: People who need to jot down a thought right now and do not store things for long. Not suited for those who switch devices or care about note preservation.

apps.title: Diary - Private Note With Lock
apps.verdict: An aesthetically pleasing journal with dated entries and attached photos. Visually appealing interface. Long entries cannot be scrolled: anything that does not fit on screen is inaccessible.
apps.loved: A visually appealing interface, chronological entry history by date, and the ability to embed photos directly in an entry.
apps.weak: Long entries cannot be scrolled: anything that does not fit on the screen is inaccessible to read. Formatting in the free version is limited to one font and one color. The lock in the app name requires the premium version.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers and young adults who want a beautiful digital journal with photos and are willing to accept the free version's limitations.

apps.title: Notes, Notepad & Memo - UpWord
apps.verdict: A color-folder notepad with gesture controls, effectively abandoned by the developer since 2018. Dropbox sync wiped all data for many users with no way to recover it.
apps.loved: Intuitive gestures: swiping to cross out a line in a shopping list. Color folders for visual organization. Convenient for lists and daily tasks.
apps.weak: Dropbox sync wiped notes for many users with no way to recover them. The developer has not responded to reports for years. The app has not been updated since 2018 and is incompatible with modern iOS versions.
apps.whoFor: No one: the app is abandoned and data in it is at risk. Historically suited those who kept color-coded shopping and to-do lists.

quotes.text: I used this app more than any other app for years and years. I had close to 200 notes. I used the app every day as my to do list, my calendar, keeping notes for my business, and my personal life.

apps.title: Diamond Diary Notes With Lock
apps.verdict: A journal with a cute visual style aimed at children. Technically weak: the screen does not scroll while typing, so the cursor slides under the keyboard. Not considered a serious note-taking tool.
apps.loved: A cute visual style with themed covers helps children want to keep a journal. Basic text input works without registration. A calendar highlights days when entries were made.
apps.weak: The screen does not scroll while typing, sending the cursor under the keyboard: you cannot see what you are writing. Accidental note deletion happens without a confirmation prompt. No content search.
apps.whoFor: Children aged 8-12 who want a pretty journal without strict privacy requirements.

apps.title: My Super Secret Diary Notes
apps.verdict: A visually appealing journal for teenagers. Includes voice memos and a variety of fonts. For some users, entries do not save after closing the app.
apps.loved: A variety of fonts and page styles. Voice memos as an alternative to text input. A simple interface that children find easy to understand.
apps.weak: For some users, entries do not save after closing the app: everything written disappears. No search across entries. Photos cannot be inserted into an entry.
apps.whoFor: Teenagers who want to keep a personal journal on their phone and are willing to pay for a lock, or parents buying the app for a child.

apps.title: iNote - Sticky Note by Color
apps.verdict: A color-coded notepad in the style of ColorNote for Android, ported to iOS. Several updates wiped all user notes without warning. In January 2026 another update silently erased data for many users by enabling auto-delete. Support does not respond.
apps.loved: Color-coded notes for fast navigation. Simple interface without extra steps. Convenient for shopping lists and everyday tasks.
apps.weak: Several waves of data loss after updates: font turned white on a white background, notes multiplied or disappeared entirely. The developer has not responded to complaints for years.
apps.whoFor: No one: storing important data in this app is dangerous. Only suitable for disposable temporary notes with no value.

apps.title: AI Note Taker - Voice to Notes
apps.verdict: A voice memo app with AI transcription and summarization. Works unreliably: long recordings are cut off or fail to transcribe entirely. Several users bought lifetime access, after which the developer renamed the tier and stopped honoring the purchase. Support does not respond.
apps.loved: When it works correctly: transcription and a brief meeting summary are ready quickly. Useful for short notes and lectures in a foreign language.
apps.weak: Recordings longer than 30 minutes regularly disappear or fail to transcribe. The app switches the transcription language to Spanish or another language on its own. Lifetime access purchases stop working after tiers are renamed.
apps.whoFor: No one in its current state. In theory it could suit students and journalists for short voice notes if it worked reliably.

apps.title: Moleskine Notebooks
apps.verdict: A companion app for the Moleskine smart pen. Since 2025 sync has effectively been shut off, support has been silent for months, and promised update dates keep slipping. Users who bought the physical notebooks cannot access their notes.
apps.loved: The concept of digitizing handwriting in real time is appealing, and in the rare cases when it worked properly users marveled at the accuracy of recognition.
apps.weak: Sync with the pen has not worked since early 2025. Data is inaccessible without the cloud. Tech support does not respond for months at a time. The app crashes when the pen is connected.
apps.whoFor: No one at this point. The ecosystem is effectively non-functional.

quotes.text:
Update OCT 22 2025

I can’t express my disappointment enough.  There was a silent decision to disable sync in Jan 2025 while working on a new improved version. So far I’ve been given 4 release dates. June of 25, Sept of 25, Oct of 25, and n

The original app was never great but it worked and I could keep my content locally without using their cloud services. This new 3.0 major update forces you to upload all of your old notes to the cloud. After updating the app, they give you no choice.
6/5/2025 EDIT: I just received a response from Moleskine saying the app had backup and cross-device functionality and I just checked it. Neither of those features work on the app.

scenarios.name: Technical specialists and researchers
scenarios.job: Build a long-term knowledge base in plain-text format with reliable sync, so the data stays readable in ten years through any change of tools.
scenarios.gap: Reviews of Obsidian and Bear describe trouble editing and syncing on the phone. Test a short correction to a note and the resolution of a conflict between devices.

scenarios.name: Medical and hard-science students
scenarios.job: Take lecture notes while creating flashcards for review at the same time, so there is no double work before exams.
scenarios.gap: Reviewers complain about notes freezing and errors after updates. A useful test: save a large set of notes, open it again, and make a flashcard out of a fragment.

scenarios.name: Managers and professionals with packed meeting schedules
scenarios.job: Want to be present in meetings rather than taking notes: they need automatic minutes with action items right after the call.
scenarios.gap: Reviewers describe recordings cutting out and trouble in a noisy room. What is needed is a recording state you can see and a way to check that the conversation was saved.

scenarios.name: Long-form writers
scenarios.job: Keep the manuscript, the drafts and the research in one place with reliable sync between phone and computer.
scenarios.gap: Reviews discuss Markdown being shown, lag in long manuscripts and lost documents. Test a long text, a clean reading mode and restoring from a backup.

scenarios.name: Personal diary writers
scenarios.job: Want to keep a personal diary regularly in a pleasant interface and to keep the entries when they change phones.
scenarios.gap: For a personal diary it is worth combining pleasant daily entry with a backup people can understand. Reviewers describe local entries lost after the app was deleted.
